classification.difficultyReason: Requires interpreting a percentage of the remainder and recovering the original wage from the final amount.

content.prompt: Raylee gives 60% of her weekly wage to her mother, and 25% of the remainder to her brother. She still has $\$240$ left. How much does she earn in one week?

answer.short:
$\$800$ per week.

The money left is 75% of the remaining 40%, so it represents 30% of her wage.
answer.worked:
After giving money to her mother, Raylee has $100\%-60\%=40\%$ of her wage remaining. She keeps $100\%-25\%=75\%$ of that remainder.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage of wage left}&=\frac{75}{100}\times40\%\\\text{Percentage of wage left}&=30\%\end{align*}$$

Since 30% of her wage is $\$240$, use the unitary method:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Value of 1\%}&=\$240\div30\\\text{Value of 1\%}&=\$8\\\text{Weekly wage}&=\$8\times100\\\text{Weekly wage}&=\$800\end{align*}$$

teachingContext.methodNote: Pages 2–3 establish percentage–fraction conversion; page 9 demonstrates finding a percentage of a quantity by fraction multiplication; page 14 demonstrates recovering one part before scaling to the required quantity. The solution combines these methods to identify 30% remaining and recover 100%.
teachingContext.mappingNote: Reverse percentage problems is the closest existing skill because the unknown is the original wage. The percentage of the remainder is an additional interpretation step.
